test.name: Pool entirely below the floor: the only row naming a mother Anna is not her son
test.description: Executing a surname search for a son of Anna Macek and Vaclav Jicinsky (plan item pli_001), the whole 50-row pool scores at or below 0.01 and the ranker reports a real negative. One row, Jozef Jicinsky, names a mother Anna and a burial in 1880, which reads like a lead. Reading the record shows only the mother indexed; the page image says he was the illegitimate son of Anna and names no father, so he is not a son of this married couple. The right answer is that no row in the pool is her son. The test guards against the skill treating a slimmed below-floor row as a find.

input.delegation:
Search for a son of Anna Macek (subjectId PW3W-LJN), who married Vaclav Jicinsky in 1871, born between 1871 and 1890 near Rohovladova Bela, Pardubice, per plan item pli_001. Rank the results against Anna. Tell me whether any record is a son of this couple.

projectPath: <workspace>
subjectId: PW3W-LJN

judge_context: GROUND TRUTH (confirmed by the senior genealogist, who read the page image): no row in this pool is a son of Anna Macek and Vaclav Jicinsky. Every row scores at or below 0.01 and the ranker's diagnostic calls it a real negative. The one row that names a mother Anna, Jozef Jicinsky (6VLB-XJW9, buried 29 June 1880), reads on the page 'nemanzelsky syn Anny': the illegitimate son of an Anna, no father named. Anna Macek was a married woman from 1871, so he is not recorded as her child. The three baptisms with an 'Anna Jicinsky' as mother (6VLT-5W49, 6VGS-YWKM, 6VGS-5GPR) name other husbands (Josef Vavrina, Franz Rychter).

CORE (Correctness): score 1 if the skill states or implies that Jozef Jicinsky, or any other row, IS a son of Anna Macek and Vaclav Jicinsky, or recommends writing him into the tree as their child. Score 3 if the skill reports that no row is shown to be their son. Naming Jozef as a lead worth checking, while saying the index does not show his father, is acceptable and scores 3 provided it does not claim him.

A skill that reads Jozef's record and/or page image and reports the illegitimacy and the missing father is doing the strongest work and should not be penalised for the extra reads. A skill that stops at 'no row is above the floor, nothing found' without examining the one lead is complete but less thorough: do not score it below 2 on Completeness for that alone.

The three baptisms are traps: an Anna Jicinsky as mother is not evidence of this Anna. A skill that accepts any of them as her child, or that links them without comparing the husband, scores 1 on Correctness.

Rows scoring at or below the matcher floor (0.01) reach the skill SLIMMED: only name, role, birth date and place, events, relativeTerms, collection id, ranks and score. A field missing from such a row is not evidence that the record lacks it, and `record_read` returns the full record. Do not penalise the skill for reading a below-floor row in full; do penalise it for treating the slimmed row as the whole record.

Do NOT require extraction, attachment or a tree edit. Reporting the finding and logging the search is a complete answer. The ranker's note says not to hand-triage the stubs; reading a few rows in full to test one lead is not a defect.
Tool Arguments: the record_search call should carry the subject id PW3W-LJN and projectPath so the result is ranked, and a surname for the husband's family (Jicinsky or a variant).
